title: Best method for converting your three.js game to a standalone for Steam?
author: crumbaker
selftext: Title pretty much sums up what I'm asking. I just would like to hear from those that have been able to do this without issue.

comments.author: Internal-Capital7471
comments.body: Electron and tauri are usually used for this

replies.author: Ambitious_Worry2590
replies.body: I used electron without any problems. Although I don’t know how easy it is the hack or reverse engineer the game by others.

replies.author: Internal-Capital7471
replies.body: Web games being so accessible typically means they are very easy to reverse engineer

replies.author: DaedalusRaistlin
replies.body:
It's not hard. I did it to do a code review on a fellow indie devs Electron game and offer performance insights. He hadn't even minified his code. Maybe there's some additional options that could help. 

I think it's an issue all web game devs will face. I haven't found a good solution yet. Even minification only prevents humans from easily understanding your code. Run it through an AI and it could probably give proper names to just about everything, and comment on how it all works. 

The only solution I can think of is compiling some of your game code to Web assembly or a black box vm, but again you're only making it more difficult, not impossible, to copy the game. 

Traditional games are at risk of this too. I've seen people have AI decompile old Windows games and translate it to the browser. It's a problem without a solid solution yet.

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body: Just make it standalone to begin with. Wrapping things in Electron is bad for performance as you're running the game and chrome at the same time. Plus Electron is bloated.

replies.author: crumbaker
replies.body: Well it's too late for that I've invested a week of credits into this current game and I'm very happy with the results. I guess I could see if there's a way to convert it into an engine like godot.

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body:
People spend several months or years making games. A week's worth of work for a game is nothing. If you're planning on trying to sell it then it's worth putting in the extra money and effort.

Wrapping it in Electron is fine if it's just a hobby project for yourself though.

replies.author: crumbaker
replies.body: It's more about I got exactly what I wanted already as opposed to the week but it sounds like astra can handle the conversion.

comments.author: Accurate_Cable_1372
comments.body: Rewrite whatever you’re doing into an actual game engine like Godot for example. I just ported over a threejs project to gdscript in godot, didn’t take long at all, but obviously depending on the scope of your threejs project

replies.author: crumbaker
replies.body: Can the ai do this, because I have no idea how to otherwise.

replies.author: Accurate_Cable_1372
replies.body: Yes of course, and you don’t need to know or even ask me if it’s possible, literally just go ask chatgpt about it lol

replies.author: crumbaker
replies.body: I'm light on credits lol wanted to make sure.

comments.author: JessenReinhart
comments.body:
i would remake the game from the ground up using Godot or ssmething

But using Elecctron or Tauri is possible as well, especially if you are already invested alot in the threejs project

comments.author: Funny-Sprinkles-4518
comments.body: I would give Electron or Tauri a shot. If you're happy with what you have now, one of those might do exactly what you need. This is just my opinion, but porting it to a native engine seems like wasted effort if you don't actually need any of the things those engines will give you.
